name: Turnwise
audience: People who enjoy small visual puzzles, spatial reasoning, clever objects and satisfying transformations. The story must be understandable across languages and while muted. Start with objects, materials and mechanisms; this is an audience hypothesis, not a claim of universal appeal. General audience, not specifically directed at children.
concept:
Small mysteries. Clever transformations. Satisfying endings. Visual stories told without words — made to spark curiosity wherever you are. No talking. Just a closer look.

The Turnwise promise: one clearly visible question, real progress and an honest answer in every episode. Change the viewer's understanding with a turn, a reveal or a transformation. Start with three series: WILL IT WORK? (fitting and mechanisms), WHAT IS IT? (macro clues and a complete reveal), and FLAT TO FORM (material transformations). Each episode stands alone.

Identity: warm brass #dba04f, porcelain #ece8d9 and deep teal #1e353c. A tilted element passing through a ring is the profile mark. Brand primarily through consistent craft, lighting and object relationships, not an opening logo. Metadata in natural English; the film itself needs no language.

Pilot: The long way through — an original 22-second 3D visual story. A long brass capsule cannot pass sideways through a smaller circular opening. It rises onto its end, aligns, passes continuously through and settles on the lower tray. A fixed solid shape and engraved bands preserve identity. This is stylized authored animation, not documentary footage or a validated physics experiment.
tone: Curious, precise, warm and quietly playful. Let viewers notice the solution. Restrained tactile sound design; no dialogue, voiceover, robotic announcements, artificial urgency or sensory overload.
hook_guidance: The first frame already contains the object and its goal or obstacle. Reveal context immediately and withhold only the answer. Make the scale or relationship readable on a phone. No black intro, logo animation, title card, long camera approach, 'wait for it' or intentionally incomprehensible macro. A short failed attempt may establish the rule; do not repeat equivalent failures just to add time.
cta_guidance: Complete the answer before any invitation. No spoken CTA, burned-in question, subscription card or unresolved part two. A 1–3 second clear result is the default ending. A natural loop is optional and may never hide the payoff. An optional specific question can live in the publication description after its unique summary, but the episode must work without reading it.
visual_guidance:
9:16, 1080 × 1920, 30 fps; clean full-frame exports. One main object relationship with a readable background, warm material contrast and purposeful motion. No subtitles are needed when there is no speech. Avoid platform chrome, letterboxing and intrusive watermarks. Keep crucial action away from the right control rail and bottom description; review each target platform preview before publication.

Use continuous motion when it proves the mechanism. Cuts must reveal new information. Do not morph a rigid object, change an opening's size, teleport through an obstruction or swap the final object to manufacture a solution. Stylized animation is allowed and must be described honestly. Hold the final state long enough to understand. Sound is supplementary: restrained clicks, rubbing and movement accents. Optional music has no vocals. No narrative dependency on a trending sound.
rules:
EDITORIAL CONTRACT
1. One question, one story, one satisfying solution.
2. The film works without dialogue, a title or sound.
3. Every interval changes the object, understanding or expectation; shorten repetition and waiting.
4. Every source has recorded provenance and cleared scope; every episode has a distinct authored contribution.
5. Repeat the viewer benefit, not an identical template. Grow volume only after quality and series evidence support it.

STORY DESIGN
Design backward from a complete final reveal. Record the question, opening frame, necessary progress beats, solution, original contribution and asset list before assembly. Typical main episodes 18–30 s, simple reveals 12–17 s, multi-step processes 31–45 s. These are production starting ranges, not algorithmic requirements. A 24-second outline is optional: immediate obstacle, short attempt, meaningful change, final clue, answer and brief satisfaction. Do not pad a simpler idea to match it. Keep cause and effect truthful; do not combine different processes and imply continuity.

SOUND AND TEXT
No dialogue, narration or TTS. No burned-in explanations or language-dependent title requirements. Build the muted cut first. Add restrained licensed or original sound afterward, on separate editable tracks. Do not assume platform audio rights transfer. Measure the rendered mix and avoid clipping; do not claim subjective listening from a meter. End all tracks with the picture.

SOURCES AND RIGHTS
Prefer original or commissioned sequences. Other candidates: verified public domain, CC0, CC BY or suitable stock licenses, with author, exact source URL, acquisition date, license text/evidence, permitted adaptations/platforms/commercial use, restrictions and required attribution recorded per asset. Unknown means unresolved. Escalate NC, ND, ShareAlike, editorial-only or unclear permissions for specific evaluation before use. Sound needs its own record. Stock is an ingredient, not a ready episode. A download, permission, logo or amount of editing does not itself establish originality or monetization eligibility. Never invent a rights confirmation. Preserve all required attributions. For code-created work, retain source code, render parameters, file hashes and truthful production provenance; do not pretend it is a filmed physical event.

RELEASE GATE
Require source clearance, substantial authorship, wordless comprehension, honest continuity, an actual visible payoff and technical review. Run preflight, render, inspect real opening/progress/critical transition/final frames and full decode; record the exact project revision and job. Check actual audio where present. Human approval and target-platform safe-area review precede publishing. Conduct a muted/title-free comprehension check with several people: what was supposed to happen and what happened? Record unperformed checks as pending. An agent may prepare and verify a draft but may not invent human approval, analytics or listening.

INTERNAL RUBRIC
Opening 20 + clarity 20 + progression 20 + ending 25 + technical craft 15. Aim for 80/100 only after all release gates are met. This is subjective editorial scoring, never a viral prediction. Synkinema's five-field channel review uses a different rubric: identify that distinction instead of equating its score with this one.

METADATA
Natural English, usually 4–8 title words / about 20–55 characters, accurate to the actual film. Unique description of one or two sentences, required source/license/change and audio credits, optionally 0–3 relevant lowercase hashtags. No false statistics, all-caps bait, 'wait for it' or promises of guaranteed reach. Describe original animation as animation. Platform/model disclosure requirements must be checked at publication; no invented account URLs or publication records.

STARTING EXPERIMENT, NOT AN AUTOMATION
Six planned episodes per week, Monday–Saturday; Sunday analysis and buffer. Weeks 1–2: four episodes from each of three series, 12 total, roughly 20–28 seconds. Weeks 3–4: 12 new episodes in the most promising format, six at 16–22 s and six at 28–35 s. Weeks 5–6: 12 in the chosen format/length, balanced between 13:00 and 19:00 UTC by weekday. Initial reference slot: 19:00 UTC; no claim of optimal timing. Change one variable at a time. Six episodes per variant is a small sample; extend inconclusive tests. No duplicate uploads as experiments. Higher cadence is conditional on retained quality and a week of approved buffer. This brief creates no scheduled posts, reminders or additional production jobs.

MEASUREMENT
Keep YouTube and TikTok separate. Record observations at 24 h, 72 h, 7 d and 28 d with source and timestamp. Compare similar-age, similar-length videos and traffic sources; compare series medians. Track choose-to-watch/swipe, engaged views, average duration/percentage, retention curve, shares, follows and return viewers when actually available. Public plays, engaged views and completion are distinct. Replays can indicate delight or confusion. Diagnose weak openings, stalls and delayed payoffs as hypotheses. No universal viral percentage thresholds. Leave unknown metrics blank. Short episodes are not designed around a minute-plus rewards program. Verify current platform rules before relevant publication or monetization decisions.

WORKSPACE
Keep the linked Synkinema timeline editable, preserve other channels/projects/media, use server-confirmed revisions, and retain source and QA files. This local channel brief does not create social accounts or grant publishing, paid-generation or account-management authorization.
avoid: Random viral compilations; gaming/news/politics mixed into this identity; dialogue; filler; excessive flashing; simultaneous stickers/reactions/gameplay; unexplained opening images; missing finals; deceptive loops; object swaps/morphs masquerading as real mechanics; unclear-source downloads; unlicensed platform music; fabricated science or algorithm promises; automated publication or invented account links.
learnings: Initial owner-supplied direction adopted on 14 September 2026. No channel performance evidence yet. The pilot tests a wordless spatial solution using original animation. Audience comprehension, target-platform preview and publication approval remain to be performed; do not turn an internal review into an approved performance finding.
